title: AI security glossary
summary: Definitions for reading and documenting AI security experiments.
html:
Token

A unit produced by a tokenizer; token counts vary by model and input.

Context window

The input and generated sequence available within a model interaction, subject to model limits.

Embedding

A numeric representation used for tasks such as similarity search. Similarity does not imply authorization.

RAG

Retrieval-augmented generation: selected external material is supplied to a model as context.

Agent

Application behavior that uses model outputs to select or request actions, often through tools.

Tool executor

The code that validates and performs a proposed action. It should enforce identity and permissions.

Prompt injection

Untrusted input influences instructions or behavior in an LLM application.

Jailbreak

An attempt to circumvent a model’s behavioral constraints; application impact needs separate analysis.

Provenance

Evidence of where data or an artifact originated and how it changed.

Canary

Synthetic identifiable data used to observe information flow without exposing real secrets.

Trust boundary

A transition where inputs from one level of authority enter a component with different privileges.

Repeatability

The extent to which a documented procedure yields the stated result under specified conditions.
